# Half-integer symmetric chains: actual centers and one-sided tilt localization

These are exact all-length reductions, not a proof of OC for the class.
They keep the center at an integer base and the one original shared tilt.

## 1. Actual deepest bases are the two central integers

Let d>=1 and let an actual finite positive-d-volume mixed source in
R x R^d be invariant under the ambient reflection(z,x)->(1-z,x).
Assume the positive fibers form a consecutive integer interval, as they
do for a convex body. Every global maximizing positive-depth base is
0 or1.

Indeed each positive fiber's depth is continuous and attains its maximum
on its compact fiber, as proved by the explicit bounded-tilt argument in
one-integer-coordinate-strict-depth-interpolation.md. There are finitely
many positive fibers, and some fiber-interior point has positive depth
from its own positive-volume contribution. Any zero-volume source fibers
are beyond the positive interval and have depth zero by a vertical tail
cap, so they cannot interfere with this maximization.

If(j,x) is a positive-depth global maximizer, reflection makes(1-j,x)
another. If j is neither0 nor1, the two integer bases differ by at least3.
The archived strict-depth-interpolation theorem then gives strictly larger
depth at a strictly intermediate integer convex combination of these two
points. That point belongs to the actual convex body and the original
mixed-integer set. This contradicts maximality.

For a common-vertex simplex source with fibers r_j T_d, coordinate
permutation symmetry and convexity of depth superlevel sets allow a
maximizer at base0 to be chosen on its diagonal. The exact movable-diagonal
comparison in candidate 44a12d13f3aabab3
then puts it at

    (0,t*1),  0<t<=R/(d+1),   R=r_0=r_1.

The reflected base1 has the same depth. Thus no half-integer candidate,
randomization, or unproved rounding is used in this localization.
This does not assert that the optimal diagonal parameter is the own
centroid endpoint.

## 2. One sign of the actual base tilt always suffices

Suppose the paired fibers satisfy K_{-h}=K_{h+1} for h=0,...,m.
Fix ANY actual point(0,x0), any nonzero continuous normal u, and define

    F_h(s)=vol_d(K_{-h} intersect{u.x>=u.x0+s}).

These tails are nonincreasing, including all their closed boundaries.
The two cap masses with opposite base tilts b and-b,b>=0, have paired
contributions respectively

    F_h(bh)+F_h(-b(h+1)),
    F_h(-bh)+F_h(b(h+1)).

Their difference is exactly

    [F_h(-b(h+1))-F_h(-bh)]
       +[F_h(bh)-F_h(b(h+1))]>=0.                 (1)

The cross-label comparison is essential. Both brackets are nonnegative
by monotonicity, without log-concavity, skewness or a density assumption.
Summing over all pairs proves that a depth minimum at base0 may be
restricted to nonpositive integer tilt. At base1 the reflected statement
restricts the tilt to be nonnegative. There is no change of integer grid.

## 3. Large tilts already satisfy OC at the central own centroid

Take the common-vertex simplex fibers

    K_{-h}=K_{h+1}=r_h T_d,  h=0,...,m,
    r_0=R>0, R>=r_1>=...>=r_m>=0,
    T_d={x_i>=0,sum_i x_i<=1}, V_d=vol_d(T_d).

Assume the sampled family is convex-compatible, for example the paired
radii form a concave sequence. Let

    y=(0,t*1),  t=R/(d+1),
    gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d,     W=sum_{h=0}^m r_h^d.

The total mixed mass is2V_d W. The desired n=1 constant is therefore
an absolute cap payment gamma_d V_d W.

The positive-normal reduction at the own centroid applies because the
sampled radius majorant r_j<=R touches at0. Normalize the nonnegative
continuous normal by sum_i w_i=1. By Section2 restrict the original
base tilt to-beta with beta>=0. The cap is

    -beta z+w.x>=t.                                (2)

If beta>=t, then at every LEFT outer fiber z=-h,h>=1, its continuous
threshold t-beta h is nonpositive. Since w.x>=0 throughout the fiber,
that entire original fiber is captured, including the equality boundary.
The own central fiber at z=0 contributes at least gamma_d R^d V_d by
ordinary Grünbaum at its actual own centroid. All other original fibers
add nonnegative mass. Therefore

    cap >=V_d[gamma_d R^d+sum_{h=1}^m r_h^d]
         >=gamma_d V_d W.                         (3)

This proves every such large-tilt cap, for every continuous dimension,
every positive normal and every number of fibers. In the same coordinates,
a purely vertical cap through base0 captures one full member from every
reflected pair, so it has mass at least V_d W>=gamma_d V_d W.

Consequently a proof at the central own centroid only needs to consider

    w_i>=0, sum_i w_i=1,     0<=beta<t,             (4)

with one common beta for every original fiber. The own-centroid claim
itself is not established by these reductions. If movable diagonal
points are required instead, the majorant swap acquires the tied roof
penalty already recorded in the movable-diagonal note; it cannot be
silently dropped.

## 4. Scope and measure

All masses here are finite sums of ordinary d-volume on original fibers.
There is positive mass because R>0. Zero-volume terminal fibers may be
omitted from the sums without affecting any closed cap mass or the actual
central points. The formulas preserve oblique couplings between the base
and continuous coordinates. No scalar layer is re-centered separately.
The reflection(z,x)->(1-z,x) preserves the integer lattice and every
fiber measure exactly. These lemmas do not settle the remaining compact
parameter set(4), do not prove that its minimum reaches the target, and
do not prove arbitrary nonsymmetric chains or general OC.

## 5. Exact straightening of a completely uncaptured terminal suffix

Specialize to d=2 and normalize a positive continuous normal to(a,1-a),
a>=1/2. Keep the actual central own centroid, t=R/3, and the worst tilt
-beta with beta>=0. Pair h is completely uncaptured in area exactly when

    a r_h+beta h<=t.                               (5)

Indeed its left threshold t-beta h is the smaller of its two thresholds,
and the maximum continuous functional on r_h T is a r_h. Equality in(5)
only adds a supporting face of zero area. The margin a r_h+beta h-t is
concave in h and is positive at h=0. Consequently its nonpositive
indices, if any, form a terminal suffix H,...,m with H>=1.

Fix the first two radii meeting that suffix, r_{H-1},r_H, and set
D=r_{H-1}-r_H>=0. For k>=H replace r_k by

    r'_k=min{r_H-(k-H)D,(t-beta k)/a}.              (6)

Keep every earlier radius fixed. Concavity of the old radius profile
gives r_k<=r_H-(k-H)D; condition(5) gives r_k<=(t-beta k)/a. Thus
r'_k>=r_k, with equality at k=H. The minimum of these two affine
functions is concave. At the join its right slope is at most-D,
the already fixed incoming slope. Both slopes are nonpositive, so the
whole replacement one-sided sequence is again nonincreasing and concave.
It remains positive wherever the original radii were positive.

Repeat the radii symmetrically at the paired original integer bases
-h,h+1. The resulting chain is still an actual convex-compatible source
with the same central fiber and the same chosen point. Every altered
pair remains completely uncaptured by(5). Thus the mass of this ONE
fixed original shared-tilt cap is exactly unchanged, while total source
mass weakly increases. Its normalized mass therefore cannot increase.

This proves a genuine finite deformation of an uncaptured terminal
suffix to at most two affine pieces. It does not classify the captured
prefix, optimize the normal or tilt, or give a theorem-strength global
localization step. If there is no empty suffix, no deformation is made.

## 6. Exact annular comparison and small-tilt payment in dimension two

Let J(beta) be the cap mass divided by V for the half-integer chain at
base0, with positive normal(a,1-a), threshold t=R/3 and worst tilt-beta.
Let I(beta) be the analogous cap mass for the actual integer-centered
symmetric chain with radii r_h at bases+/-h and one central radiusR.
The latter is a convex-compatible source by the same radius concavity,
and its actual central own centroid is the SAME continuous point.
Its total mass divided by V is2W-R^2, where W=sum_{h=0}^m r_h^2.
Directly grouping the right fibers gives the exact identity

    J(beta)-I(beta)
      =sum_{h=1}^m[F_{a,r_{h-1}}(t+beta h)
                         -F_{a,r_h}(t+beta h)]
         +F_{a,r_m}(t+beta(m+1))=:E(beta)>=0.        (7)

Each bracket is the cap area of the genuine annulus
r_{h-1}T minus r_hT. These disjoint annuli and the inner r_mT partition
RT up to null boundaries. Each of their thresholds is at most
t+beta(m+1). Consequently

    E(beta)>=F_{a,R}(t+beta(m+1)).                  (8)

The explicit triangular tail has derivative magnitude at most2R/a<=4R
on every piece, including the repeated-height endpoint directions.
It is globally continuous and piecewise differentiable, so this gives
a global Lipschitz bound. Ordinary triangle Grünbaum supplies
F_{a,R}(t)>=gamma_2 R^2, gamma_2=4/9. Therefore

    E(beta)>=gamma_2 R^2-4R beta(m+1).              (9)

If0<=beta<=R/[18(m+1)], the right side is at least gamma_2 R^2/2.
The completed integer-centered symmetric triangle-chain theorem gives

    I(beta)>=(gamma_2/2)(2W-R^2)

at the actual peak own centroid for every original shared tilt. Adding
(9) proves

    J(beta)>=gamma_2 W,

which is exactly OC for the original even chain of total mass2V W.
The annular identity and all constants remain finite when some terminal
radii vanish; zero area terms can simply be deleted.

Combining Sections3 and6 proves every positive-normal cap at the central
own centroid except the explicit remaining tilt window

    R/[18(m+1)] < beta < R/3.                     (10)

No uniform lower bound E(beta)>=gamma_2 R^2/2 is claimed beyond the
small-tilt range; even the two-fiber case disproves it at large beta.
The displayed exact payment is an all-length result, but it does not
yet control the intermediate window(10) or prove the whole half-integer
symmetric chain theorem.
